title: The Hollow Spire Again
premise: Emrys Sandoval, a royal food-taster and secret charm-seller in a kingdom that outlawed magic seven years ago, has survived by being forgettable—until a mute child appears at their door speaking the dead tongue of Vael, a country erased from every map and memory. The child is a living key to the Hollow Spire, the last door out of Vael, which still exists somewhere beneath the capital's foundations. As Emrys deciphers the language through fragments of their own suppressed childhood memories, they discover they were born in Vael and their immunity-building was never accidental: the crown has been using tasters like them to slowly poison the last Vaeli bloodlines into extinction. To save the child—and themselves—Emrys must betray the queen who sheltered them, unseal the Spire during the solstice eclipse, and choose between erasing their own memories of Vael forever or carrying a truth that could reignite a war. In the end, Emrys sends the child through alone, keeps the memories, and remains behind as the first witness of a country that officially never existed.
about_author: Petra Eriksen is a former archivist from Bergen who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes about people who survive by hiding what they know.

chapters.title: The Taster's Table
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A routine morning tasting the queen's breakfast establishes Emrys's careful invisibility: the numb tongue, the ledger of poisons survived, the charms sold discreetly after dark. When a knock comes at dusk and a silent child stands there speaking words no one should know, Emrys's carefully constructed anonymity cracks. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine, ending with the first word Emrys somehow understands.

chapters.title: A Language Without a Country
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys hides the child, Cora, among the spice stores and consults a disgraced linguist, Master Ivo, who identifies the speech as High Vaeli—a language outlawed alongside magic. Ivo warns that speakers were purged; the child shouldn't exist. That night Emrys dreams in Vaeli for the first time. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into fear as Emrys realizes the dream-words feel like remembering, not learning.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Investigating the taster corps' records, Emrys finds gaps: seven years ago pages were removed, and every taster hired since carries a Vaeli surname. The realization lands that the 'immunity program' is a slow poisoning of survivors. Meanwhile Captain Sere, the queen's spymistress, begins asking why a food-taster receives strange visitors. Emotional beat: betrayal—the institution that saved Emrys was the trap all along.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Confession
chapters.summary: Cora's POV, rendered through fragmented, sensory perception without language. Through Cora's eyes we see Emrys's small kindnesses and small cowardices, the city's watchful windows, and Cora's own fading memories of the Spire—a tower of doors that hums. Cora remembers being sent to find 'the one who tastes.' Emotional beat: tenderness and guilt; Emrys sees themself truly for the first time.

chapters.title: Master Ivo's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo agrees to help translate Cora's recitations in exchange for Emrys smuggling his forbidden research out of the capital—but he confesses he helped design the purge's linguistic census, marking every Vaeli speaker for removal. His guilt makes him unreliable; Sere has already approached him. Emotional beat: complicity and the question of whether helping now can ever balance what was done before.

chapters.title: Beneath the Foundations
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Following Cora's humming map through cisterns and sealed streets, Emrys finds the Hollow Spire's outer door buried under the palace itself—guarded by wards keyed to royal blood. They learn the solstice eclipse will briefly unlock it. Sere catches Emrys returning at dawn but says nothing, watching. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by surveillance; the door exists, and so does the noose.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Queen
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Summoned before Queen Isolde, Emrys expects arrest—instead the queen reveals she knows about Vael, about Cora, about everything. She offers mercy: surrender the child, drink a final draught that will erase Emrys's Vaeli memories, and live honored. Her loneliness is genuine; her mercy is a cage. Emotional beat: the loyalty-versus-truth theme crystallizes—Emrys loves the queen and must defy her.

chapters.title: The Longest Night Before
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Emrys, Ivo, Sere. On the eve of the eclipse, Ivo is taken by Sere's agents; Emrys must choose to flee with Cora or attempt a rescue. Sere, revealed as a Vaeli survivor who chose the crown, confronts Emrys: forgetting is survival, she insists. Emrys refuses. Emotional beat: grief and resolve—every ally costs something, and Emrys stops calculating and starts choosing.

chapters.title: The Eclipse at the Spire
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. During the eclipse, Emrys breaches the Spire using their own tainted blood—seven years of poison have made them the only key the wards cannot refuse. Sere arrives to stop them; Ivo, escaped, holds the guards with a final act of translation that reawakens the tower's sleeping voice. The door opens onto a country that still breathes beyond it. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice, defiance, and wonder fused.

chapters.title: The One Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Only one can pass before the door seals for another generation. Emrys sends Cora through with a recorded testimony of everything the crown did, keeping their own memories despite the cost. Weeks later, Emrys resumes tasting the queen's food—now an open secret, a living witness. Rumors of Vael begin to stir in taverns. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; truth survives in one stubborn rememberer.
